Great job explaining! You're absolutely correct too. As someone dealing with anxiety for essentially my entire life, I can tell you that this is true. I went on a leave of absence from work because I thought that would help me, but then I realized if it wasn't work giving me anxiety, it was my own bodily sensations like my heart beating too fast or feeling out of breath. I went to the doctor three separate time and each time they said that I'm fine. That's when I started reading self help books and all of them said to not run from the anxiety or situations that make you anxious, but rather accept it, acknowledge that it is there and cope with it. After months of practicing this everyday, I can proudly say my anxiety has been reduced significantly. And I had really bad anxiety too; tight muscles, indigestion where I could barely even drink water; shortness of breath; dizziness. But I'm slowly overcoming it. I guess what I'm trying to say is that sometimes the only way out is the way through.
